reason: Long explainers are where this niche pays and where small channels break in (a 12.7K-subscriber channel's 'inside an AI chip' video passed 1M); Shorts are thinner than geography and the biggest Shorts are 3D skits we can't make.
conditions: Long-first: 1 long video a week, 12-16 minutes ('what happens inside X when you Y'), with Shorts as trailers for it
Build an 'inside view' kit before sample 1: exploded layers, zoom through scales (phone -> chip -> transistor), signals flowing along paths, on the flat kit; true 3D only if the stills fail
Every claim sourced (manufacturer docs, papers, reputable press); no rumours, no AI hype stated as fact, no product reviews
The full research measures only on-niche videos: the scan pulled in 3D 'what's inside' cutaways, anatomy and Hindi engineering channels (about 30 of 45 channels)
for: Small channels win long: 4 of 8 tech channels under 100K subscribers had a long video at 5x their median; Silicon Up Close (12.7K subs) has 1.02M, 447K and 270K views on 15-20 minute 'what happens inside' videos
Tech long videos: median 23.5K views in 90 days (73 videos), 21% of them hits; the 600-900 s band hits 19% of the time
Rising and evergreen: AI, chips and Starlink explainers from 2-5 months ago still lead (Starlink 4.6M, sea cable maker 5.5M)
against: Tech Shorts: median only 4.0K views in 90 days (267 Shorts), against 20K for the geography niche; small channels' Short hits top out around 50-160K
The biggest Shorts (Professor Of AI, 10-18M each) are 3D character skits; neither that nor Branch Education's 3D cutaways is what our flat kit draws today
Crowded at the top: ColdFusion, Branch Education, Asianometry and Business Insider each pull 230K-1.2M median on long

earnings.assumptions: Estimates, not sourced figures: 1 long video a week + 2 Shorts a day; tech/education long-video RPM roughly $4-10 per 1,000 views (commonly reported creator ranges; an estimate) and Shorts about $0.05; the partner programme by 1,000 subs + 4,000 watch hours around month 4-7 if a few long videos reach 5-20K views; 'high' needs one long video near the 1M a small channel has reached

demand.smallChannelsWithHit: 7/18 Shorts, 4/8 long (tech titles only, channels under 100K subs)
demand.note: Medians over tech-titled videos only; scan.json's whole-scan medians (Shorts 11.6K, long 5.9K) include off-niche 3D, anatomy and Hindi channels

doable.look: partly: animated diagrams on the flat kit fit (flows, layers, zooms); the hits' look is 3D cutaways and 3D character skits, so an 'inside view' kit must be built and judged on sample 1's stills
doable.voice: yes: English, a Kokoro US narrator
doable.policy: fine: advertiser-friendly; rules against rumours and AI-hype claims; no AI label needed for drawn animation
